notes: Curated CIK/ticker identity evidence for the 30-control universe. Every record must cite a checkable primary source, and no CIK may be written from recollection. Statuses follow the approved evidence hierarchy: MANUAL_VERIFIED requires a human-checked filing citation; RESOLVED is reached by sec_company_tickers or filing_document_text; name matching and full-text search can never establish a mapping on their own. Absence of evidence is recorded as absence. Dated lifecycle facts are scope-tagged and kept out of valid_from/valid_to, which mean generic ticker validity and are a broader claim than any single filing supports. Verified so far: AAPL, GM (both issuers). Run `tradeit edgar verify-control <ID> --index-root <DIR>` to gather candidates for the rest.

controls.notes: The easy case, and the pilot's baseline. One issuer, continuously listed, currently trading, so the SEC's own company_tickers.json is authoritative for the CURRENT CIK-to-ticker relationship. Recorded as RESOLVED rather than MANUAL_VERIFIED: sec_company_tickers is sufficient primary SEC evidence under the approved ranking, while MANUAL_VERIFIED stays reserved for a human-checked filing citation. valid_from and valid_to are deliberately null — the ticker file proves the mapping as of its retrieval date and says nothing about which historical dates AAPL was valid, and the filing spine corroborates issuer continuity without dating the ticker.

mappings.citation: SEC company_tickers.json, https://www.sec.gov/files/company_tickers.json, retrieved 2026-08-14; exactly one AAPL match: {"cik_str": 320193, "ticker": "AAPL", "title": "Apple Inc."}
mappings.scope_notes: issuer + security_class + exchange_listing all continuous; no identity break observed. Independently corroborated by the local SEC full-index: CIK 320193 carries 2,232 filings spanning 1994-08-12 to 2026-08-13 under the registrant names APPLE COMPUTER INC, APPLE COMPUTER INC/ FA, APPLE INC and Apple Inc., which is a rename of one registrant rather than a succession of issuers. Many weaker name-match candidates containing APPLE exist in the index; CIK 320193 is the one the SEC ticker reference corroborates directly, so the mapping rests on sec_company_tickers and the index serves only as corroboration.

controls.notes: The hard case. Pets.com listed in February 2000 and wound up in November 2000, so it appears in no current SEC ticker file and EDGAR full-text search does not reach back to 2000. EDGAR can establish that a registrant of this name existed and filed, and can supply its CIK; what it cannot easily supply is the TICKER, because EDGAR is CIK-centric and 2000-era filings do not carry an authoritative ticker field. This control is expected to end at AMBIGUOUS or UNRESOLVED, and that is the honest outcome rather than a failure. A ticker read off a prospectus cover page would be FILING_DOCUMENT_TEXT evidence and could support RESOLVED; a ticker recalled from memory is not evidence at all.

mappings.scope_notes: issuer lifecycle establishable from EDGAR; exchange_listing lifecycle is the hard part
mappings.unresolved_reason: sec.gov unreachable from the authoring environment. Verification route: locate the registrant in the local EDGAR full-index for 1999-2001 to obtain the CIK, then read the S-1/424B cover page for the proposed Nasdaq symbol (evidence filing_document_text, citation = accession). If no filing states the symbol, this control stays UNRESOLVED and is reported as such.

controls.expected_company: General Motors Corporation (pre-2009) and General Motors Company (2010-)
controls.notes: Two distinct registrants that shared the ticker GM across a bankruptcy roughly a year apart. They must never be merged: doing so produces exactly the spliced series that full-01 already failed on with BBBY, and a one-CIK-per-control model cannot express the break at all. Each issuer carries its own CIK and evidence, and identity_break is true so the merge cannot happen by accident. Note the asymmetry the two records preserve: old GM's ISSUER lifecycle continued through bankruptcy and liquidation long after its EXCHANGE LISTING ended, so those two scopes close at different times and are recorded separately. Neither issuer carries a valid_from or valid_to: the evidence establishes CIK-to-ticker relationships and one dated exchange-listing removal, and none of it dates generic ticker validity at either end.

mappings.citation: SEC Form 10-K for fiscal 2008, GENERAL MOTORS CORP, CIK 40730, accession 0001193125-09-045144 (local copy gm-2009-10k.txt), manually inspected: the filing states the registrant's common stock was listed under the trading symbol "GM" on the New York Stock Exchange
mappings.scope_notes: General Motors Corporation, later Motors Liquidation Company. The CIK-to-ticker relationship rests on filing-document evidence manually inspected, not on name matching. valid_to is deliberately null: the July 2009 NYSE removal is an EXCHANGE-LISTING fact and is recorded as a lifecycle fact rather than as generic ticker validity, because a Form 25-NSE proves removal from one exchange and does not prove the symbol could never appear in another venue or context afterwards. This is emphatically not the issuer's corporate death date -- old GM continued as a legal entity through the bankruptcy and liquidation process.

lifecycle_facts.fact: NYSE stated its intention to remove General Motors Corporation common stock from listing and registration on the Exchange at the opening of business on July 20, 2009, following the Company's June 1, 2009 voluntary Chapter 11 filing and the Exchange's determination that the securities were no longer suitable for continued listing and trading.
lifecycle_facts.citation: SEC Form 25-NSE, accession 0000876661-09-000303, filed by NEW YORK STOCK EXCHANGE INC for issuer GENERAL MOTORS CORP (CIK 40730), security: Common Stock
lifecycle_facts.note: This is the common-stock Form 25-NSE. It is NOT accession 0000876661-09-000262, which concerns the 1.50% Series D Convertible Senior Debentures due June 1, 2009 and must never be cited as the common-stock lifecycle evidence.

lifecycle_facts.fact: SGML header EFFECTIVENESS DATE of the common-stock Form 25-NSE.
lifecycle_facts.citation: SEC Form 25-NSE, accession 0000876661-09-000303, document header field EFFECTIVENESS DATE: 20090708
lifecycle_facts.note: Recorded separately and deliberately NOT equated with the body-stated removal date of 2009-07-20. They are different fields making different claims, and collapsing them would silently pick one.

mappings.scope_notes: General Motors Company: a separate registrant with its own CIK that later held the ticker GM. RESOLVED rather than MANUAL_VERIFIED, matching the AAPL precedent -- manually viewing the SEC ticker JSON does not make it a filing citation, and the evidence hierarchy is preserved. Independently corroborated by the local SEC full-index: CIK 1467858, General Motors Co, 2,138 filings spanning 2009-07-16 to 2026-08-11. Its filing history is entirely separate from CIK 40730's and must never be concatenated with it. valid_from is null: the ticker file dates nothing, and the first filing date is not the date the ticker was acquired.
